nu.etymology: From Latin nōn. Compare Romanian nu.

cum.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *quomo, from Latin quōmodo.

os.etymology: From Latin ossum, from os. Compare Romanian os.

vi.etymology: Cf. the corresponding ni for noi. Compare Romanian vă. Compare also Italian vi

amar.etymology: From Latin amārus. Compare Romanian amar.

or.etymology: From Latin ōrō. Compare Daco-Romanian ura, urez.

pi.etymology: From Latin per. Compare Romanian pe.

el.etymology: From Latin ille, possibly through a Vulgar Latin *illus. Compare Romanian el, Megleno-Romanian iel.

an.etymology: From Latin annus. Compare Romanian an.

her.etymology: From Latin ferrum. Compare Daco-Romanian fier, Spanish hierro.

pom.etymology: From Latin pōmus. Compare Daco-Romanian pom.

son.etymology: From Latin sonus. Compare Daco-Romanian sun.

car.etymology: From Latin carrus, from Gaulish *karros. Compare Romanian car.

glosses_en: alternative form of anot to swim

bat.etymology: From Latin battō, from earlier battuō. Compare Daco-Romanian bat, bate.

ver.etymology: From Latin (cōnsobrīnus) vērus. Compare Romanian văr.

vers.etymology: From Latin versō. Compare Romanian vărsa, vars.

leg.etymology: From Latin ligō. Compare Romanian lega, leg.

alas.etymology: From Latin laxō. Compare Romanian lăsa, las.

mal.etymology: Cognate to Daco-Romanian mal. From Proto-Albanian *mala (“mountain”) (Albanian mal). Proto-Albanian *mal- reflecting an ancient Balkan toponym. See Albanian mal (“mountain”) for more.

sin.etymology: From Latin sinus. Compare Romanian sân, Spanish seno.

chin.etymology: From Latin pīnus. Compare Romanian pin.

bag.etymology: Either of substrate origin or from a Vulgar Latin *begō, from Late Latin bīgō, from Latin bīga. Less likely from Greek βάζω (vázo, “put in, set on”). May have originally referred to putting animals under a yoke. Compare Romanian băga, bag.

shed.etymology: From Latin sedeō. Compare Romanian ședea, șed.

spun.etymology: From Latin expōnō. Compare Romanian spune, spun.

lem.etymology: From Latin lignum. Compare Daco-Romanian lemn.

sap.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *sappō, from Latin sappa. Compare Romanian săpa, sap, French saper, Italian zappare, Sicilian zappari, Spanish zapar, Friulian sapâ, Venetan sapar, Latin sappa.

u.etymology: Probably from an early (proto-Romanian) root *eaua, from Latin illam, accusative feminine singular of ille. Compare Romanian o.

ore.etymology: From Latin hōra. Compare Romanian oară.

lui.etymology: From Late Latin illūi, which is a form of Latin illī (dative singular of ille). Compare Romanian lui.

ni.etymology: From Vulgar Latin nīs, from Latin nos. Compare Romanian ne (older form nă).

un.etymology: Inherited from Latin ūnus. Compare Romanian un.

ping.etymology: Probably from Latin impingō, with the loss of the initial prefix, or from a root *pingō instead of pangō. Compare Daco-Romanian împinge, împing.

ta.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *ta, from Latin tua, feminine of tuus. Compare Romanian ta.

mer.etymology: From Late Latin mēlum, from Latin mālum. Compare Daco-Romanian măr.

fag.etymology: From Latin fāgus. Compare Romanian fag.

li.etymology: From Latin illis, dative common plural of ille. Compare Romanian le.

ar.etymology: From Latin arō. Compare Daco-Romanian ara, ar.

ti.etymology: Inherited from Latin tē, accusative of tū. Compare Romanian te.

pot.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin *pot(e)o, analogical replacement for possō, regularization of Latin possum. Compare Romanian pot, putea.

la.etymology: From Latin illac. Compare Romanian la.

ac.etymology: Inherited from Latin acus. Compare Romanian ac.

es.etymology: From Latin exeō. Compare Daco-Romanian ieși, ies.

tu.etymology: From Latin tū, from Proto-Italic *tū, from Proto-Indo-European *túh₂.

vache.etymology: From Latin vacca. Compare Romanian vacă.

alb.etymology: From Latin albus. Compare to Daco-Romanian alb.

gras.etymology: Inherited from Late Latin grassus. Compare Romanian gras.

bash.etymology: Inherited from Latin bāsiō (“to kiss”). This is one of relatively few words for which the Daco-Romanian equivalent (in this case săruta) is not derived from the same Latin word.

cash.etymology: From Latin cāseus. Compare Romanian caș.

meal.etymology: From Albanian mal, cognate to Aromanian mal and Romanian mal with the same origin.

ea.etymology: From Latin illa, feminine of ille. Compare Romanian ea.

noi.etymology: From Latin nōs. Compare Romanian noi.

voi.etymology: Inherited from Latin vōs, from Proto-Italic *wōs. Compare Romanian voi.

mini.etymology: From Latin mē, possibly through Vulgar Latin mēne (a root), or through analogy with tsini, from *quene, from quem. Compare Romanian mine, also Dalmatian main.

pat.etymology: From Latin patior. Compare Daco-Romanian păți.

nec.etymology: From Latin necō. Compare Daco-Romanian îneca, înec.

cos.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *cōsō, from Latin consuō. Compare Romanian coase, cos.

code.etymology: From Vulgar Latin coda, from Latin cauda. Compare Daco-Romanian coadă.

cot.etymology: From Latin cubitum. Compare Daco-Romanian cot.

est.etymology: Inherited from Latin esse. Forms beginning with h- are derived from corresponding forms of Latin fierī.

bes.etymology: Inherited from Latin vissiō. Compare Romanian băși.

beau.etymology: From Latin bibō. Compare Romanian bea, beau.

ed.etymology: From Latin haedus. Compare Romanian ied.

sum.etymology: From Latin subtus, from sub. Compare Romanian sub.

rob.etymology: From a Slavic language, from Proto-Slavic *orbъ (“slave”). Compare Romanian rob.

cornu.etymology: Inherited from Latin cornū. Cognate with Romanian corn.

surd.etymology: From Latin surdus. Compare Romanian surd.

per.etymology: From Latin pilus. Compare Romanian păr.

lung.etymology: From Latin longus. Compare Romanian lung.

tor.etymology: From Latin tornō. Compare Romanian turna, torn.

neg.etymology: Probably from Latin mergō. Compare Romanian merge, merg.

nel.etymology: From Latin ānellus. Compare Romanian inel.

nou.etymology: From Latin novus. Compare Romanian nou.

yin.etymology: From Latin veniō. Compare Romanian veni, vin.

di.etymology: From Latin dē. Compare Romanian de.

orb.etymology: From Latin orbus. Compare Romanian orb.

lumi.etymology: From Latin lūmen. See figurative meaning as the "light of life". Compare Megleno-Romanian lumi and Romanian lume.

pap.etymology: Inherited from Latin pappus, from Ancient Greek πάππος (páppos).

cap.etymology: From Vulgar Latin capus, from Latin caput. Plural form capiti from Latin capita. Compare Romanian cap.

che.etymology: From Latin quod. Compare Romanian că.

Italia.etymology: Definite form of Italii; -a (feminine definite article) added on.

hic.etymology: From Latin fīcus. Compare Megleno-Romanian ic, Spanish higo.

vale.etymology: From Latin vallis, vallem. Compare Romanian vale.

bun.etymology: From Latin bonus. Compare Daco-Romanian bun.

cad.etymology: From Late Latin cadeō, cadēre, from Latin cadō, cadĕre. Compare Daco-Romanian cad, cădea.

cher.etymology: From Latin pereō. Compare Romanian pier(i).

ou.etymology: Inherited from Classical Latin ōvum, possibly via Vulgar Latin (*)ŏvum. Compare Romanian ou, Sicilian ovu.

par.etymology: From Latin pāreō. Compare Daco-Romanian părea, par.

ma.etymology: From Latin magis. Compare Romanian mai.

sec.etymology: From Latin siccus. Compare Romanian sec.

piper.etymology: From Greek πιπέρι (pipéri), from Ancient Greek πέπερι (péperi).

sac.etymology: From Latin saccus. Compare Romanian sac.

fur.etymology: From Vulgar Latin fūrō, from Latin fūror. Compare Romanian fura, fur.

porc.etymology: From Latin porcus. Compare Romanian porc.

abat.etymology: Akin to synonymous Romanian abate (“to stray”). Perhaps from Late Latin abbattō (“to beat down, strike”), for which compare bat (“to beat, strike”).

tun.etymology: From Latin tonō. Compare Romanian tuna, tun.

plug.etymology: From a Slavic language, compare Proto-Slavic *plugъ, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *plōgaz, *plōguz (“plough”). Compare also Daco-Romanian plug.

hir.etymology: From Latin fīlum. Compare Daco-Romanian fir.

dor.etymology: From Latin doleō. Compare Romanian durea.

lac.etymology: From Latin lacus (“lake”), from Proto-Indo-European *lókus (“lake, pool”).

mort.etymology: From Latin mortuus. Compare Romanian mort.

strop.etymology: Probably from Latin stroppus, from Ancient Greek στρόφος (stróphos, “rope”), from στρέφω (stréphō, “to twist”).

crest.etymology: From Latin crēscō. Compare Romanian crește, cresc.

crier.etymology: Probably from Latin cerebrum through Vulgar Latin *crebrum or possibly from the diminutive form cerebellum through a root *crebellum (compare the variant form, also found in Megleno-Romanian, which seems to still preserve the -l-). Compare

tut.etymology: From Latin tōtus. Compare Romanian tot.

mai.etymology: From Latin Maius or Greek Μάιος (Máios). Compare Romanian mai.

putrid.etymology: From Latin putridus. Compare Romanian putred.

tai.etymology: From Late Latin taliō, from Latin talea. Compare Romanian tăia, tai.

minti.etymology: From Latin mentem, accusative singular of mēns, from Proto-Indo-European *méntis. Compare Romanian minte.

nod.etymology: From Latin nōdus. Compare Daco-Romanian nod.

sul.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *sublum, from *sūbulum, from Late Latin insūbulum, from Latin insuō + -bulum, or related to sūbula.

drum.etymology: Borrowed from Greek δρόμος (drómos, “road, track”). Compare Romanian drum.

dau.etymology: From Latin dō. Compare Daco-Romanian da, dau.

vin.etymology: From Latin veniō. Compare Daco-Romanian veni, vin.

cred.etymology: From Latin crēdō. Compare Romanian crede, cred.

abur.etymology: Akin to Romanian abur, Albanian avull, dialectal Greek άμπρος (ámpros), άμπουρους (ámpourous) of unclear origin, though most often derived from Albanian, see there for more.

lai.etymology: Uncertain. Compare Romanian lai, Albanian ljaj.

alt.etymology: From Latin alter, alterum. Compare Romanian alt.

mor.etymology: From Latin morior. Compare Romanian mor, muri.

min.etymology: From Latin minō, collateral form of minor. Compare Romanian mâna, mân.

fut.etymology: From Latin futuō. Compare Romanian fute, fut.

gol.etymology: Probably borrowed from Old Church Slavonic голъ (golŭ), from Proto-Slavic *golъ (“naked”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gelH- (“naked, bald”). Compare Romanian and Megleno-Romanian gol, Bulgarian гол (gol), Serbo-Croatian go, gol.

mea.etymology: From Latin mea. Compare Romanian mea.

elu.etymology: From Latin ille, possibly through a Vulgar Latin *illus. Compare Romanian el.

une.etymology: From Latin ūna, feminine of ūnus.

torc.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *torcō, from Latin torqueō. Compare Romanian toarce, torc.

mosh.etymology: Uncertain; possibly a substratum term or related to Albanian moshë. Compare Romanian moș.

vas.etymology: From Latin vāsum. Compare Daco-Romanian vas.

tsi.etymology: From Latin quid. Compare Romanian ce.

stat.etymology: Borrowed from Italian stato or Latin status.

mari.etymology: Probably from an irregular shortened form of maior, maiōrem (“bigger”); alternatively from Latin mās, marem (“male”), with a shift in meaning. Compare Megleno-Romanian mari and Romanian mare, and see there for a more detailed etymology.

scot.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *excotō, from Latin excutiō. Compare Romanian scoate, scot.

rog.etymology: From Latin rogō. Compare Romanian ruga, rog.

cali.etymology: From Latin callis, callem. Compare Romanian cale.

fug.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *fugō, from Latin fugiō. Compare Romanian fugi, fug.

nat.etymology: From Latin nātus (“born”). Compare Romanian nat (“personal, individual”).

fluir.etymology: From or related to fluiarã / fluearã. Compare Romanian fluiera, fluier.

sari.etymology: From Vulgar Latin sale, from Latin sāl, salem. Compare Romanian sare.

pri.etymology: From Latin per. Compare Romanian pe (archaic pre).

unu.etymology: From Latin ūnus, from Old Latin oinos, from Proto-Italic *oinos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos (“one, single”).

rug.etymology: From Latin rubus. Compare Romanian rug.

stari.etymology: From stau or from Latin stāre. Compare Romanian stare.

duc.etymology: From Latin ducō. Compare Romanian duce, duc.

fet.etymology: From Latin fētō. Compare Daco-Romanian făta.

vom.etymology: From Latin vomō. Compare Romanian voame, vom.

plop.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *ploppus from classical Latin pōpulus. Compare Romanian plop.

parti.etymology: From Latin pars, partem. Compare Romanian parte.

sus.etymology: Inherited from Latin sūsum. Compare Romanian sus.

peni.etymology: From Latin pānis, pānem. Cognate with Romanian pâine.

nes.etymology: Probably from an earlier form *cun ãsu, from Vulgar Latin *cum ipso, from *ipsus or Latin ipsum, from ipse, or from metathesis of a form *ãns. Compare Romanian dânsul, îns.

spes.etymology: From Latin spissus. Compare Italian spesso.

afin.etymology: From Latin daphne, with loss of initial 'd', from Ancient Greek δάφνη (dáphnē, “laurel”). Compare Romanian afin, also Calabrian afina ("laurel").

lat.etymology: Ultimately from Latin lātus; cf. Romanian lat.

ashi.etymology: From Late Latin ac sīc; compare Romanian așa.

amari.etymology: From Latin mare, from Proto-Italic *mari, from Proto-Indo-European *móri. Compare Daco-Romanian mare.

seu.etymology: Inherited from Latin sēbum. Compare Romanian seu.

arcu.etymology: From Latin arcus. Compare Romanian arc.

scad.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *excadeō, from Latin ex- + cadō. Compare Daco-Romanian scădea, scad.

gros.etymology: From Latin grossus. Compare Romanian gros.

puts.etymology: From Latin puteus. Compare Romanian puț.

foc.etymology: From Latin focus. Compare Romanian foc.

shi.etymology: From Latin sic. Compare to Daco-Romanian și.

vã.etymology: Cf. the corresponding nã for noi. Compare Romanian vă.

lã.etymology: From Latin illīs, dative common plural of ille. Compare Romanian le.

doi.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *dui (“two”, root), from Latin duo, from Proto-Italic *duō, from Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁. Compare Romanian doi.

fundu.etymology: From Latin fundus. Compare Daco-Romanian fund.

sud.etymology: Borrowed from French sud. Compare Romanian sud.

cunji.etymology: Ultimately from Latin cūnae. This form perhaps came through Greek κούνια (koúnia).

brats.etymology: From Latin brachium, bracchium, from Ancient Greek βραχίων (brakhíōn). Compare Romanian braț.

albastru.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin *albaster, albastrum root, derived from Latin albus (“white”). Compare Romanian albastru.

cal.etymology: From Late Latin caballus (“horse”), from Latin caballus (“pack horse”). Compare Romanian cal.

frig.etymology: From Latin frīgus. Compare Daco-Romanian frig.

anin.etymology: Probably from a Vulgar Latin *alīnus, from *alnīnus, from Latin alnus + -īnus. Compare Romanian anin, Megleno-Romanian rin.

rar.etymology: From Latin rārus (“seldom”). Compare Romanian rar.

limpid.etymology: From Latin limpidus. Compare Romanian limpede.

pisti.etymology: From Latin per + super. Compare Romanian peste.

piros.etymology: From per + -os or from Latin pilōsus. Compare Romanian păros.

lupu.etymology: From Latin lupus from an Osco-Umbrian language, from Proto-Italic *lukʷos, metathesis of Proto-Indo-European *wĺ̥kʷos. Compare Romanian lup.

mur.etymology: Inherited from Latin mūrus, from Old Latin *moerus, *moiros, from Proto-Indo-European *mey- (“to strengthen”).

bou.etymology: From Latin bōvem, accusative singular of bōs, possibly through a Vulgar Latin *bovum root. Compare Daco-Romanian bou.

fum.etymology: From Latin fūmus. Compare Romanian fum.

glosses_en: minute, small, fine, short, slim, thin, etc.

crep.etymology: From Latin crepō. Compare Romanian crăpa, crăp.

meni.etymology: From Latin māne. Compare Daco-Romanian mâine.

oie.etymology: From Latin ovem, accusative of ovis. Compare Romanian oaie.

lor.etymology: From Latin illōrum (“of those”), genitive plural of ille, illud. Compare Romanian lor.

hiu.etymology: Inherited from Latin sum. The citation form and the h- conjugations come from Latin fīō (“become”). Compare Romanian fi.

tru.etymology: From Latin intro. Compare Romanian întru.

greu.etymology: Inherited from Early Medieval Latin grevem, alteration of Latin gravem. Compare Romanian greu.

negru.etymology: From Latin nigrum. Compare Daco-Romanian negru.

mult.etymology: From Latin multus. Compare Romanian mult.

mut.etymology: From Latin mūtō. Compare Romanian muta, mut.

lume.etymology: From Latin lūmen. See figurative meaning as the "light of life". Compare Romanian lume.

trei.etymology: From Latin trēs, from Proto-Italic *trēs, from Proto-Indo-European *tréyes. Compare Romanian trei.

patru.etymology: From Latin quattuor, quattor, from Proto-Italic *kʷettwōr, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷetwóres. Compare Sardinian batero, batoro, batro, baturu, Romanian patru.

hig.etymology: From Latin īnfīgō or fīgō. Compare Romanian înfige, înfig.

loc.etymology: From Latin locus. Compare Daco-Romanian loc.

tac.etymology: From Latin taceō. Compare Romanian tăcea, tac.

ved.etymology: From Latin videō. Compare Romanian vedea, văd.

lut.etymology: From Latin lutum. Compare Romanian lut.

lau.etymology: From Latin lavō. Compare Romanian la, lau.

imn.etymology: Probably from Vulgar Latin *amblō, itself from Latin ambulō. Compare Romanian umbla, umblu, Megleno-Romanian amnu.

fac.etymology: Inherited from Latin faciō. Cognate with Romanian face.

arem.etymology: Probably from Latin rimō. Compare Romanian râma, râm.

arad.etymology: From Latin rādō. Compare Romanian rade, rad.

aras.etymology: From Latin rāsus. Compare Romanian ras.

nai.etymology: From Latin nāvis. Compare archaic Romanian naie.

fus.etymology: From Latin fūsus. Compare Romanian fus.

metur.etymology: From meturã. Compare Romanian mătura, mătur.

moli.etymology: From Latin mollis, mollem. Compare Romanian moale.

frati.etymology: From Latin frāter. Compare Romanian frate.

cumnat.etymology: From Latin cognātus (“related by blood”). Compare Romanian cumnat, Dalmatian comnut, Albanian kunat.

socru.etymology: From Late Latin socrus m, from Latin socer, from Proto-Indo-European *swéḱuros. Compare Romanian socru.

glosses_en: Turkey (a country located in Eastern Thrace in Southeastern Europe and Anatolia in West Asia)
Turchia.etymology: Definite form of Turchii; -a (feminine definite article) added on.

uin.etymology: From Latin ovīnus. Compare Romanian oină.

asun.etymology: From Latin sonō. Compare Romanian suna, sun.

anot.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *notō, from Latin natō. Compare Romanian înot.

ares.etymology: From Latin rīsus. Compare Romanian râs.

surin.etymology: From soari or possibly from Vulgar Latin *solīnus (“sunny”), from Latin sol. Compare Megleno-Romanian surin.

glosses_en: unfermented wine; grape or other fruit juice
mustu.etymology: From Latin mustum. Compare Romanian must.

aeri.etymology: From Latin herī. Compare Daco-Romanian ieri.

mamã.etymology: From Latin mamma. Compare Daco-Romanian mamă.

stur.etymology: Uncertain. Possibly from Latin stylus, stilus. Compare Romanian stur. Cf. also Albanian shtyllë.

vali.etymology: From Latin vallis, vallem. Compare Romanian vale.

glosses_en: dark-green; black-green; color between green and black
gangur.etymology: From Latin galgulus, from galbulus, from galbus (“yellow”). Compare Romanian grangur (“oriole”), Sicilian gàjulu (“golden oriole”), Spanish gálgulo, compare also Albanian gargull.

sclav.etymology: Borrowed from Medieval Latin sclavus (“slave”), from Late Latin Sclavus (“Slav”). Doublet of shcljau.

slab.etymology: From a Slavic language, ultimately from Proto-Slavic *slàbъ. Compare Romanian slab, Bulgarian and Macedonian слаб (slab), Serbo-Croatian slȁb.

vrut.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *volūtum, past participle for Latin volēre. Compare Romanian vrut.

trag.etymology: From Early Medieval Latin tragō, from Latin trahō. Compare Romanian trage, trag.

stric.etymology: Ultimately from Latin extricō; cf. Romanian strica, stric.

avut.etymology: Past participle of am. From Vulgar Latin *habūtus, replacing Classical Latin habitus.

dinte.etymology: From Latin dēns, dentem. Compare Romanian dinte.

lucredzu.etymology: Probably from Latin lucror with the Aromanian suffix -edzu, or less likely ultimately from Latin lūcubrō. Compare Romanian lucra, lucrez.

cunoscu.etymology: From Late Latin conōscō, variant of Latin cognōscō. Compare Romanian cunosc.

porche.etymology: From Latin porca. Compare Romanian poarcă.

cãntu.etymology: From Latin cantō. Compare Romanian cânt.

-tor.etymology: From Vulgar Latin -torius, -torium, and feminine -toari, toare from Vulgar Latin -toria, -toriam, both from Latin -tor. Ultimately from Proto-Italic *-tōr, from Proto-Indo-European *-tōr < *-tor-s.

optu.etymology: From Latin octō, from Proto-Indo-European *oḱtṓw. Compare Romanian opt.

lunã.etymology: From Latin lūna, from Old Latin losna, from Proto-Italic *louksnā, from Proto-Indo-European *lówksneh₂, from Proto-Indo-European *lewk-. Compare Romanian lună.

apã.etymology: From Latin aqua. Compare Romanian apă.

funi.etymology: From Latin fūnis, fūnem. Compare Romanian funie.

matsin.etymology: Inherited from Late Latin māchinō (“mill, grind”), a verb based on Latin māchina (“device, mill”), an early borrowing from Ancient Greek. Compare Romanian măcina, macin.

vultur.etymology: Inherited from Latin vultur or vulturius. Compare Romanian vultur.

tini.etymology: From Latin tē, as with mini. Compare Romanian tine.

glosses_en: dark blue, bluish-grey in color, violet-blue in color
vinit.etymology: From Latin venetus (“sea-colored, bluish; Venetian”). Compare Romanian vânăt.

murar.etymology: From moarã + -ar or from Latin molārius. Compare Romanian morar.

ofitsial.etymology: Borrowed from Latin officialis. Compare to Daco-Romanian oficial.

limbã.etymology: From Latin lingua, from Old Latin dingua, from Proto-Italic *dn̥ɣwā, from Proto-Indo-European *dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s. Compare to Romanian limbă.

oclju.etymology: From Vulgar Latin oclus, from Latin oculus; compare to Daco-Romanian ochi.

tser.etymology: From earlier tsel, from Latin caelum. Compare Daco-Romanian cer.

albu.etymology: From Latin albus. Compare to Daco-Romanian alb.

ãnveastã.etymology: From Slavic, from Proto-Slavic *nevěsta. Compare to Daco-Romanian nevastă.

sãndze.etymology: From Vulgar Latin sanguem, alteration of Latin sanguinem, accusative of sanguis. Compare to Daco-Romanian sânge.

lunjinã.etymology: From Latin lūmina, plural of lūmen. Compare to Daco-Romanian lumină.

ghine.etymology: From Latin bene. Compare to Daco-Romanian bine.

lacãrmã.etymology: From Latin lācrima. Compare Daco-Romanian lacrimă, lacrămă.

ular.etymology: From oalã + -ar or from Late Latin ollārius, from Latin olla. Compare Romanian olar.

mascur.etymology: From Latin masculus. Compare to Daco-Romanian mascur.

agiutor.etymology: From Latin adiūtōrium. Compare to Daco-Romanian ajutor.

furnigã.etymology: From Latin formīca. Compare to Daco-Romanian furnică.

frãndzã.etymology: From Late Latin frondia n pl, a collective noun derived from Classical Latin frondeus (“leafy”). Compare Romanian frunză.

glosses_en: in an Aromanian way; as the Aromanians do

sots.etymology: From Latin socius. Compare Romanian soț.

frec.etymology: From Latin fricō. Compare Daco-Romanian freca, frec.

sug.etymology: From Latin sūgō. Compare Romanian suge, sug.

educatsie.etymology: Borrowed from Latin educatio. Compare to Daco-Romanian educație.

adzã.etymology: From Latin hāc die, reduced to local Vulgar Latin *hadie, probably through confusion with hodie. Compare Romanian azi.

altu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *altru, from Latin alter, alterum. Compare Romanian alt.

ãn.etymology: From Latin in. Compare Romanian în and Sicilian 'n.

fãrã.etymology: From Latin foras. Compare to Daco-Romanian fără.

hilj.etymology: From Latin fīlius. Compare Daco-Romanian fiu, Spanish hijo.

prublemã.etymology: From Latin problema (probably a borrowing), from Ancient Greek πρόβλημα (próblēma).

revistã.etymology: From Italian rivista through Romanian revistă.

tati.etymology: From Latin tata. Compare Daco-Romanian tată.

Gãrtsia.etymology: Definite form of Gãrtsii; -a (feminine definite article) added on. Ultimately from Latin Graecia. Compare Romanian Grecia.

glosses_en: Spain (a country in Southern Europe, including most of the Iberian peninsula)
alternative form of Ipir: Epirus (a historical region and ancient kingdom in Southeastern Europe, today split politically between northwestern Greece and southwestern Albania)
Epirus (a geographic region and administrative region in northwest Greece, one of the thirteen peripheries of modern Greece)

arici.etymology: From Latin erīcius. Compare Romanian arici.

prived.etymology: From pri- + ved; compare Romanian prevedea, prevăd, French prevoir.

frut.etymology: Borrowed from Greek φρούτο (froúto). Ultimately from Latin fructus.

aze.etymology: From Latin hāc die, reduced locally to Vulgar Latin *hadie, probably through confusion with hodie. Compare Romanian azi.

drac.etymology: From Latin dracō, from Ancient Greek δράκων (drákōn). Compare Megleno-Romanian and Daco-Romanian drac.

virin.etymology: From Latin venēnum, either directly or via the later form venīnum. Compare Romanian venin.

vindu.etymology: From Latin vēndō. Compare Romanian vinde, vând.

njeri.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *melem, from Latin mellem, accusative of mel. Compare to Romanian miere.

platan.etymology: From Greek πλάτανος (plátanos). Compare the doublet paltin. Cf. also Romanian platan.

aprir.etymology: From Latin Aprīlis. Compare to Romanian prier, popular variant form of the standard aprilie. Cf. also Albanian prill.

glosses_en: Danube (a river in Europe; flowing 2,850 kilometers from the confluence of the Breg and Brigach at Donaueschingen, Germany, through Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova, and Ukraine, into the Black Sea)
Duna.etymology: Probably ultimately from Latin Danubius. See Danube. Compare Greek Δούναβης (Doúnavis), Bulgarian and Serbo-Croatian Дунав, Romanian Dunăre.

diparti.etymology: From di + parti. Compare Romanian departe.

diparte.etymology: From di + parti. Compare Romanian departe.

aros.etymology: From Latin rōsus. Compare Romanian ros.

alj.etymology: From Latin allium. Compare regional Romanian ai.

buti.etymology: From Late Latin buttis, probably of Ancient Greek origin. Compare Romanian bute.

ardu.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *ārdō, from Latin ārdeō. Compare Romanian ard.

curat.etymology: From the past participle of cur or possibly Latin cūrātus. Compare Daco-Romanian curat.

luminari.etymology: From Late Latin lūmināria, neuter plural of lūmināre, from Latin lūmen (“light”). Compare Romanian lumânare.

glosses_en: to gather, collect, assemble, bring together
adun.etymology: From Latin adūnō. Compare Romanian aduna, adun.

vinos.etymology: From vinã + -os or from Latin vēnōsus. Compare Romanian vânos.

murdar.etymology: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish مردار (murdar), ultimately from Persian مردار (mordâr).

zbor.etymology: Borrowed from a South Slavic language, most likely Macedonian збор (zbor, “word”), where the transformation from "meeting, gathering" to "word" occurred in the same way as the Aromanian synonym cuvendã (“word”) from Latin conventum or Alban

pulpos.etymology: pulpã + -os, or possibly from Late Latin pulpōsus, from Latin pulpa.

pulmu.etymology: From Latin pugnus. Compare Romanian pumn.

stau.etymology: From Latin stō. Compare Romanian sta, stau.

vulpi.etymology: From Latin vulpēs, vulpem. Compare Romanian vulpe.

lutos.etymology: From lut + -os or from Latin lutōsus. Compare Daco-Romanian lutos.

cãsãbã.etymology: From Turkish kasaba, from Ottoman Turkish قصبه, from Arabic قَصَبَة (qaṣaba).

arãu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin rius (“river”), from Latin rīvus (“brook, small stream”). Compare to Gascon arriu, Sardinian arriu, Romanian râu.

usos.etymology: Either from os + -os or from Late Latin ossuōsus, from Latin os. Compare Romanian osos.

buin.etymology: From bou, or possibly from Latin bovīnus. Compare old Italian buino, Occitan boïn, Catalan buina. The (Daco-) Romanian bovin is a borrowing from Latin.

maiu.etymology: From Latin Maius or Greek Μάιος (Máios). Compare Romanian mai.

agustu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin agustus, from Latin augustus. Compare Romanian agust.

nichi.etymology: From Latin neque. Compare Romanian nici.

coc.etymology: From Late Latin cocō, from Latin coquō. Compare Daco-Romanian coc, coace.

prun.etymology: From Latin prūnus, from Ancient Greek προύνη (proúnē).

tusi.etymology: From Latin tussis, tussem. Compare Romanian tuse.

merdu.etymology: Probably from Italian merda, cf. French merde. Ultimately from Latin merda.

argat.etymology: From Ottoman Turkish ارغاد (ırgat), from Ancient Greek ἐργάτης (ergátēs).

furnicar.etymology: Probably from Vulgar Latin *formīcārium, from Latin formīca. Compare Romanian furnicar.

niau.etymology: From Latin nix, nivem. Compare Romanian nea.

seti.etymology: From Latin sitis, sitem. Compare Romanian sete.

mortu.etymology: From Latin mortuus. Compare Romanian mort.

sharpi.etymology: From Vulgar Latin serpes, from Latin serpēns. Compare Romanian șarpe.

satur.etymology: From Latin saturō. Compare Romanian sătura, satur.

tsin.etymology: From Latin cēnō. Compare Romanian cina, Sicilian cinari.

-ame.etymology: From Latin -āmen. Compare Italian -ame. Cf. also -imi and Romanian -ime.

cuib.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *clubium, from Ancient Greek κλυβίον (klubíon). Compare Romanian cuib.

musafir.etymology: From Ottoman Turkish مسافر (müsâfir, “guest”), from Arabic مُسافِر (musāfir, “traveller”).

foame.etymology: From Latin famēs. Compare Romanian foame.

paltin.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *plātinus, from Latin platanus (“plane tree”), itself from Ancient Greek πλάτανος (plátanos).

apoi.etymology: From Latin ad post. Compare Romanian apoi.

pescu.etymology: From Latin piscis, probably made into a singular form analogically from the variant peashti. Compare Romanian pește, Istro-Romanian peşt. Compare also Albanian peshk, Dalmatian pasc, and Istriot piso.

iou.etymology: Inherited from Late Latin eo, from Classical Latin egō̆.

pingu.etymology: Probably from Latin impingō, with the loss of the initial prefix, or from a root *pingō instead of pangō. Compare Daco-Romanian împinge, împing.

codru.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *codrum, possibly from a variant of Latin quadrum (“square”) and Latin quadra (“morsel”). Compare Romanian codru, Albanian kodër.

surdu.etymology: From Latin surdus. Compare Romanian surd.

orbu.etymology: From Latin orbus. Compare Romanian orb.

singur.etymology: From Latin singulus. Compare Romanian singur.

gãljinã.etymology: From Latin gallina. Compare Romanian găină.

bucium.etymology: From Latin būcinum, having lost the original meaning; compare, however, the secondary sense of Romanian bucium.

cã.etymology: From Latin quod. Compare Romanian că.

sorã.etymology: From Latin soror, possibly through a Vulgar Latin *sora. Compare Daco-Romanian and Megleno-Romanian soră.

areati.etymology: From Latin aries, arietem. Compare Romanian arete.

iuva.etymology: From iu (“where”) + -va. Compare the similar construction in Romanian undeva (“somewhere”).

oai.etymology: From Latin ovem, accusative of ovis. Compare Romanian oaie.

mãn.etymology: From Latin maneō. Compare Daco-Romanian mânea, mân.

sterp.etymology: Possibly ultimately from Byzantine Greek στέριφος (stériphos). Alternatively, it may be derived from Vulgar Latin *exstirpus or Vulgar Latin *extirpus, from Latin exstirpo. Compare Romanian sterp, Albanian shterp, probably from the same sou

macru.etymology: From Latin macrum, accusative singular of macer.

arinos.etymology: From Latin arēnōsus, or from arinã + -os. Compare Romanian arinos.

glosses_en: co-father-in-law (e.g. father of a son or daughter-in-law)
cuscru.etymology: From Latin cōnsocerum, accusative of cōnsocer. Compare Daco-Romanian cuscru.

glosses_en: Forms adjectives and nouns indicating origin or place of birth (such as from a certain city or region).

capit.etymology: From an alteration of Latin capita, or a derivative of cap (“head”). Compare Romanian capăt.

timpuriu.etymology: From Latin temporivus (“early, early in the season”), ultimately from tempus. Compare Romanian timpuriu.

chior.etymology: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish كور (kör), from Persian کور (kur).

mãnã.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *mana, from Latin manus. Compare Romanian mână, Megleno-Romanian mǫnă, Istro-Romanian măre.

nari.etymology: From Latin nāris. Compare Daco-Romanian nară.

escu.etymology: From forms of Latin sum and fiō. Compare Romanian fi.

mucos.etymology: Either from muc + -os or from Late Latin mūcōsus, from Latin mūcus.

gustu.etymology: From Latin gustus, from Proto-Italic *gustus, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵéwstus. Compare Romanian gust.

versu.etymology: From Latin versō. Compare Romanian vărsa, vars.

glosses_en: to jump, leap, hop, bounce, skip
saltu.etymology: From Latin saltō. Compare Romanian sălta, salt.

fructu.etymology: Borrowed from Latin fructus. Compare Romanian fruct.

glosses_en: to behave, act a certain way, comport oneself
portu.etymology: From Latin portō. Compare Romanian purta, port, Sicilian purtari.

aestu.etymology: Probably from a Vulgar Latin *eccum istum, accusative singular of *eccum iste, from Latin eccum + iste, or alternately from Latin ad + istum. Compare Romanian acest (compare also the regional variant aiest, however).

curti.etymology: From Latin cōrtem, accusative of cōrs, shortened form of cohors. Compare Romanian curte and Sicilian curti ~ curtigghiu.

ficior.etymology: Probably from Vulgar Latin *fētiolus, from Latin fetus. Compare Romanian fecior.

glosses_en: to suck in, sip, drink in, gulp
sorbu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *sorbiō, from Latin sorbeō. Compare Romanian sorb.

beu.etymology: From Latin bibō. Compare Romanian bea, beau.

trec.etymology: From Latin trāiciō. Compare Romanian trece, trec.

soari.etymology: From Latin sōl, sōlem, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *sóh₂wl̥. Compare Romanian soare.

aspar.etymology: Possibly from Vulgar Latin *expaoreō, *expavoreō from Latin expaveō, from Latin ex- + pavor. Compare Romanian speria, Megleno-Romanian spar, spăreari, also Italian spaurire, spaurare.

ansar.etymology: From Latin saliō (with the Aromanian prefix an added). Compare Romanian sări, sar.

glosses_en: goatskin bag filled up with oil or wine

nior.etymology: From Latin nūbilum, noun use of the neuter of the adjective nūbilus (“cloudy”), from Latin nūbēs, Compare Romanian nor.

dinti.etymology: From Latin dēns, dentem. Compare Romanian dinte.

chilar.etymology: Borrowed from Greek κελάρι (kelári) (compare also Albanian qilar), itself from Late Latin cellarium. Compare the synonym and doublet tsilar, inherited from the same Latin source.

glosses_en: flat, level (as in an open country)
shes.etymology: Ultimately from Latin sessus. Cf. Romanian șes, and also Albanian shesh.

apun.etymology: From Latin appōnō. Compare Romanian apune, apun.

licurici.etymology: Compare Romanian licurici. Related to licur and licuredz.

disi.etymology: From di + si < Latin dē + sī.

glosses_en: to plunder, pillage, sack, rob, loot
prad.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *praedō, from Latin praedor. Compare Romanian prăda, prad.

blid.etymology: From Common Slavic bljudŭ. Compare Romanian blid.

luntri.etymology: From Latin lunter, luntrem, variant of linter. Compare Romanian luntre.

cãndu.etymology: From Latin quandō. Compare Romanian când.

aclo.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *eccum illōc, whence also Romanian acolo, (dialectal) aclo.

multu.etymology: From Latin multus. Compare Romanian mult.

nishti.etymology: From Latin nesciōquid. Compare Romanian niște, Megleno-Romanian niște.

lungu.etymology: From Latin longus. Compare Romanian lung, Italian lungo, Sicilian longu.

largu.etymology: From Latin largus. Compare Romanian larg.

njic.etymology: Probably from a Vulgar Latin *miccus, from Ancient Greek μῑκκός (mīkkós, “small”), variant of μικρός (mikrós). Compare Megleno-Romanian and Romanian mic and Sicilian nicu.

shcurtu.etymology: Probably from a Vulgar Latin root *excurtus, from Latin curtus. Probably influenced by Albanian shkurt, itself also probably from the same Latin root or an earlier borrowing from proto-Eastern Romance. Compare Romanian scurt.

bãrbat.etymology: From Latin barbātus. Compare Romanian bărbat.

broascã.etymology: Probably from a Vulgar Latin root *brosca, from *broscus, possibly related to Ancient Greek βροτάχος (brotákhos), whence also broatic. Compare Romanian broască, Albanian breshkë.

hilje.etymology: From Latin fīlia. Compare Romanian fie.

putsãn.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin *putinus (attested in Medieval Latin pusinnu, pittinus (“small”)), a blend of Late Latin pitinnus (“very small”) and the root of Classical Latin putus (“young boy”), putillus (“very small”). Compare Romanian puțin, Megle

tatã.etymology: From Latin tata. Compare Daco-Romanian tată.

primuvearã.etymology: Inherited from Late Latin prīma vēra (“early spring”), derived from Latin ver (“spring”). Compare Romanian primăvară, Albanian pranverë, Italian primavera.

armãneascã.etymology: From armãn + -eascã, feminine of -escu. Compare Romanian românească.

glosses_en: Aromanian (of or pertaining to Aromanians, the Aromanian language or the Aromanian culture)
armãn.etymology: Inherited from Latin rōmānus. Compare Daco-Romanian român (c-o form in older times rumân, both were used), Istro-Romanian rumăr. The initial a- is a common phonological development in Aromanian words deriving from Latin words beginning with

cãntic.etymology: From Latin canticum. Compare Romanian cântec.

featã.etymology: From Latin fēta (“woman who has just given birth”), substantivization of the adjective fētus. Compare Romanian fată.

piduclju.etymology: From Late Latin peduclus, from peduculus, from Latin pediculus, from pedis. Compare Romanian păduche, Megleno-Romanian piducľu, Istro-Romanian peducľu.

yermu.etymology: From Latin vermis. Compare Romanian vierme, Megleno-Romanian ghermi, Sicilian vemmu, vermu, Venetan vermo.

popul.etymology: From Latin populus. Compare Romanian popor.

cheptu.etymology: From Latin pectus, from Proto-Italic *pektos, from Proto-Indo-European *peg- (“breast”). Compare Romanian piept, Megleno-Romanian kľeptu.

cicior.etymology: From Late Latin petiolus, from a root *pediciolus, diminutive of Latin pedīculus, diminutive of pēs. Compare Daco-Romanian picior.

gioc.etymology: From Latin jocus, iocus. Compare Romanian joc.

virghirã.etymology: Probably from Latin virgō, virginem. Compare Romanian vergură.

glosses_en: stick used in the rolling of the warp over the roller of the loom
virdzeauã.etymology: From Late Latin virgella, diminutive of Latin virgula, itself a diminutive of virga. Compare Megleno-Romanian virdzeauă, Romanian vergea.

pãne.etymology: From Latin pānis, pānem. Cognate with Romanian pâne.

ngustu.etymology: From Latin angustus. Compare Daco-Romanian îngust; compare also Albanian ngushtë.

fumelj.etymology: From the plural of fumealji. Compare also Albanian fëmijë ("child"). The relationship with this word is uncertain; the Albanian may be a borrowing directly from Latin or from an Eastern Romance/Romanian language.

vatãm.etymology: Probably from Latin victimō. Compare Daco-Romanian vatăm, vătăma.

scriu.etymology: From Latin scribō. Compare Romanian scrie, scriu.

simintsã.etymology: From Late Latin sementia, plural of sementium, neuter form derived from Latin sēmentis, itself derived from sēmen (“seed”). Compare Romanian sămânță, Megleno-Romanian siminţă.

tsicoarã.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *cichōria, from Latin cichōrium, ultimately from Ancient Greek κιχόριον (kikhórion). Compare Romanian cicoare.

caftu.etymology: From Latin captō. Compare Daco-Romanian căuta, caut.

lemnu.etymology: From Latin lignum. Compare Romanian lemn.

arpã.etymology: From Latin alapa (“blow, slap, smack”), or ālipēs, ultimately from āla. Compare Daco-Romanian aripă.

alavdu.etymology: From Latin laudō. Compare Romanian lăuda, laud. Compare also Albanian lëvdoj.

dzãc.etymology: From Latin dicō. Compare Daco-Romanian zice, zic.

coadã.etymology: From Vulgar Latin coda, from Latin cauda. Compare Daco-Romanian coadă.

peanã.etymology: From Latin penna. Compare Romanian pană.

Njercuri.etymology: From Latin (diēs) Mercuriī. Compare Romanian miercuri.

cãlcãnju.etymology: From Latin calcāneum. Compare Daco-Romanian călcâi.

numã.etymology: From Latin nōmen, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁nómn̥. Compare Romanian nume.

zburãscu.etymology: Uncertain. Probably from Proto-Slavic *sъborъ (“gathering, meeting”); compare Macedonian збор (zbor). Not related to Daco-Romanian zbura (“to fly”); the cognate to that word in Aromanian is azboair. Possibly related indirectly to Romanian s

chiatrã.etymology: From Latin petra, from Ancient Greek πέτρα (pétra). Compare Romanian piatră.

mãc.etymology: From Latin mandūcō. Compare Daco-Romanian mănânc, mânca.

lingurã.etymology: From Latin lingula. Compare Daco-Romanian lingură.

tsarã.etymology: From Latin terra. Compare Romanian țară.

pimintu.etymology: From Latin pavimentum, possibly through attested Vulgar Latin paumentum. Compare Romanian pământ and Istro-Romanian pemint.

suptu.etymology: From Latin suctus. Compare Romanian supt.

usãc.etymology: Probably from Latin exsūcō. Compare Romanian usca, usuc.

schic.etymology: From Latin spīcum, alternative form of spīca. Compare Romanian spic.

schin.etymology: From Latin spīnus. Compare Romanian spin.

schinos.etymology: From schin + -os, or from Latin spīnōsus. Compare Romanian spinos.

toamnã.etymology: From Latin autumnus, with a change in gender as with iarã through analogy with vearã or primuvearã, possibly through an intermediate Vulgar Latin *otumna (a root), or [tempora] autumna. Compare Romanian toamnă.

vearã.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *vēra, from Latin vēr (“spring”). Compare Megleno-Romanian veară, Romanian vară.

spumã.etymology: From Latin spūma. Compare Romanian spumă.

aspum.etymology: From Latin spūmō. Compare Romanian spuma.

cãmpu.etymology: From Latin campus. Compare Romanian câmp.

astingu.etymology: From Latin extinguō. Compare Romanian stinge, sting.

shuir.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *sūbilō, from Latin sībilō, or possibly influenced by fluir. Compare Romanian șuiera, șuier.

arniclju.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin *reniclus, from contraction of Latin rēniculus (“little kidney”), from rēnēs (“kidneys”), from ren. Compare Daco-Romanian rinichi, Sardinian arrigu.

asud.etymology:
Inherited from Latin sūdō. With typical Aromanian "a" prefixing.
Compare Romanian asuda, asud.

shoaric.etymology: From Latin sōricem, accusative singular of sōrex. Compare Romanian șoarece, șoarec.

prunã.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *prūna, feminine singular formed from the neutral plural of Latin prūnum, from Ancient Greek προῦμνον (proûmnon). Compare Daco-Romanian prună (“plum”).

alumtã.etymology: Inherited from Late Latin lū̆cta. Cognate with Romanian luptă. See also the variant form ljuftã, which was either borrowed directly from or influenced by Albanian luftë.

tãrdziu.etymology: From Late Latin tardīvus, from Latin tardus. Compare Romanian târziu.

frapsin.etymology: From Latin fraxinus. Compare Daco-Romanian frasin, regional frapsăn.

vinã.etymology: From Latin vēna. Compare Romanian vână.

vimtos.etymology: From vimtu + -os, or from Latin ventōsus. Compare Romanian vântos.

bitãrnu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin or Late Latin vetrānus, syncopated form of Latin veterānus. Compare Romanian bătrân.

dzidzitar.etymology: From dzeadzit + -ar or from Late Latin digitāle, from Latin digitālis. Compare Romanian degetar.

atumtsea.etymology: From Latin ad + *tunce, archaic form of tunc. Compare Romanian atunci, atuncea.

atuntsi.etymology: From Latin ad + *tunce, archaic form of tunc. Compare Romanian atunci, atuncea.

stãrnut.etymology: From Latin sternūtō. Compare Romanian strănuta, strănut.

doamnã.etymology: From Late Latin domna < Latin domina. Compare Romanian doamnă.

agiut.etymology: From Latin adiūtō. Compare Romanian ajuta, ajut.

giur.etymology: From Latin iūrō, jūrō. Compare Romanian jura, jur.

ultu.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *oblītāre, a frequentative based on Latin oblīvīscor (via its past participle oblītus). Compare Romanian uit.

azvingu.etymology: From Latin vincō, with a prefix added later. Compare Romanian învinge, înving.

frãngu.etymology: From Latin frangō. Compare Romanian frânge, frâng.

frãmtu.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *frānctus, from Latin frāctus. Compare Romanian frânt, Italian franto.

aspargu.etymology: From Latin spargō. Compare Romanian sparge, sparg.

glosses_en: to shatter, snap, split, cleave, break
disic.etymology: Maybe from Latin dissecō or Latin despicō. See also dischic.

plec.etymology: From Latin plicō. Compare Romanian pleca, plec.

surpu.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *subrūpō, from Latin rūpes. Compare Romanian surpa, surp, Megleno-Romanian sărup, old Abruzzese dialect surrupare, Sicilian sdirupari. Compare also Italian dirupare, Spanish derribar.

alag.etymology: Possibly from a Vulgar Latin *allargō root, from Latin largus, or from a derivation of legāre, or alegāre. Compare Romanian alerga, alerg.

ãnsar.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *insalō, or *salāre with the suffix ãn later added, from a change in conjugation of Latin saliō (“to salt”). Compare Romanian săra, Romansh ensalar, ansalar.

glosses_en: to guard, watch, watch over, watch out for, keep vigil, monitor
aveglju.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *viglō, from Latin vigilō. Compare Romanian veghea, veghez.

pungu.etymology: From Latin pungō. Compare Romanian împunge, împung (archaic form punge, pung).

agiungu.etymology: From Latin adiungō. Compare Romanian ajunge, ajung.

tindu.etymology: From Latin tendō. Compare Romanian întinde, întind (older tinde, tind).

glosses_en: to spread or stretch over a surface
ashternu.etymology: From Latin asternō. Compare Romanian așterne, aștern.

aduc.etymology: From Latin addūcō. Compare Romanian aduce, aduc.

ashtergu.etymology: From Latin extergō. Compare Daco-Romanian șterge, șterg.

aleg.etymology: Inherited from Latin allegere (“choose; recruit”). Compare Romanian alege, aleg.

ntsernu.etymology: From Latin cernō, with a prefix n- added later. Compare Romanian cerne, cern.

cãrbuni.etymology: From Latin carbō, carbōni. Compare Romanian cărbune.

tsiresh.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *ceresius, from Late Latin cerasius, from Latin cerasus, from Ancient Greek κέρασος (kérasos). Compare Romanian cireș.

tsireashã.etymology: From Vulgar Latin ceresia, from the neuter plural of Late Latin ceresium, from Latin cerasium, from Ancient Greek κεράσιον (kerásion, “cherry”), from κερασός (kerasós, “bird cherry”), ultimately possibly of Anatolian origin. Compare Romania

tsinushã.etymology: From Vulgar Latin root *cinusia, from Latin cinus, a less common variant of cinis (“ashes”). Compare Romanian cenușă.

feminine singular of vrut (feminine singular past passive participle of voi used as an adjective)

minduescu.etymology: Probably from a derivation of minti (“mind”) with the suffix -escu.

mulgu.etymology: From Latin mulgeō. Compare Romanian mulge, mulg.

neauã.etymology: From Latin nix, nivem. Compare Romanian nea.

tornu.etymology: From Latin tornō. Compare Romanian turna, torn.

torcu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *torcō, from Latin torqueō. Compare Romanian torc.

glosses_en: to wring out, extort from, extract
astorcu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *extorcere, ultimately from Latin torqueō. Compare Romanian stoarce.

stricor.etymology: Probably from a Vulgar Latin root *extracolō, from Latin colō (“filter, strain, purify”). Compare Romanian strecura, strecor.

minciunedzu.etymology: From minciunã + -edzu or from a Vulgar Latin root *mentionō (with the Aromanian suffix -edzu), probably ultimately from an alteration of Latin mentior (past participle mentītus) through the influence of mentiō.

minciunã.etymology: From Late Latin mentiō, mentiōnem (in the alternative sense of "lie" as opposed to "mention"); this meaning may derive from a reduction of a root *mentītiō, from Latin mentītus, past participle of mentior, and is unrelated to the original m

lutsescu.etymology: Ultimately from Latin luceō. Compare Romanian lucesc.

arãd.etymology: From Late Latin rīdo, from Latin rīdeo. Compare Daco-Romanian râd.

arsu.etymology: From Latin ārsus, past participle of ārdeō. Compare Romanian ars, Sicilian arsu, Italian arso.

glosses_en: to watch, look look at, regard, behold, observe
mutrescu.etymology: Borrowed from Proto-Slavic *motriti, with the suffix -escu as a fourth conjugation verb.

nverdu.etymology: Possibly from ãn + veardi or from a Vulgar Latin root *invir(i)dō, from Latin viridis.

nvirdzãscu.etymology: From veardi or from a Vulgar Latin root *invir(i)dēscō, from Latin viridēscō. Compare Romanian înverzi, înverzesc.

fãpturã.etymology: From Latin factūra. Compare Romanian făptură; compare also Albanian fytyrë.

ncãldzãscu.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *incalidēscō, from Latin calidus. Compare Romanian încălzi, încălzesc, Megleno-Romanian ạncălzǫs.

friptu.etymology: From Latin frīctus. Compare Romanian fript.

furtunã.etymology: Probably from Latin fortūna or alternatively Greek φουρτούνα (fourtoúna). Compare Romanian furtună. Compare also Albanian furtunë.

njergu.etymology: From Latin mergō. Compare Romanian merge, merg.

meastic.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *mixticō, derived from Latin mixtus (“mixed”). Compare Romanian mestec.

yiptu.etymology: From Latin victus. Compare Romanian vipt, Italian vitto.

flivrar.etymology: From Late Latin Febrārius from Latin (mensis) Februārius; possibly through the intermediate of Greek Φλεβάρης (Fleváris), or influenced by it later. Compare Romanian făurar.

foarficã.etymology: From Latin forficem, accusative singular of forfex. Compare Romanian foarfecă.

adavgu.etymology: From Latin adaugeō, later changed to a first conjugation verb as with Daco-Romanian adăuga, adaug.

anvets.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin *invitiāre (“to become accustomed to”), from Latin vitium (“vice”). Compare Romanian învăța, învăț.

aveari.etymology: From the verb am/amu or from Latin habēre. Compare Romanian avere.

vreari.etymology: From Vulgar Latin volēre, regularized from Latin velle. Compare Romanian vrere.

aspel.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *experlavō, from Latin perlavō. Compare Daco-Romanian spăla, spăl.

pãstrescu.etymology: From Greek παστρεύω (pastrévo). Compare Albanian pastroj, Daco-Romanian păstra.

tushescu.etymology: From Latin tussīre, with the Aromanian suffix -escu or through a later Vulgar Latin or early Romance root *tussēscō as with most other fourth conjugation verbs. Compare Romanian tuși, tușesc, also Italian tossire, tossisco.

ampar.etymology: From Late Latin impālō, from Latin pālus. Compare Daco-Romanian împăra.

puteari.etymology: From the verb pot or Vulgar Latin potēre < Latin possum. Compare Romanian putere.

cãnut.etymology: From Late Latin cānūtus, from Latin cānus. Compare Romanian cărunt.

shtiu.etymology: Inherited from Latin sciō. Compare Romanian știu.

strimtu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *strinctus, from Latin strictus. Compare Romanian strâmt, Neapolitan strinto.

tsini.etymology: Probably from a Vulgar Latin *quene, from Latin quem, from qui. Compare Romanian cine.

nãs.etymology: Probably from an earlier form *cun ãsu, from Vulgar Latin *cum ipso, from *ipsus or Latin ipsum, from ipse, or from metathesis of a form *ãns. Compare Romanian dânsul, îns.

nãsã.etymology: Probably from Vulgar Latin *cum ipsa, from Latin ipsa, from ipse (as with the masculine nãs), or from metathesis of a form *ãnsã. Compare Romanian dânsa, însă.

elj.etymology: From Latin illī, nominative masculine plural of ille. Compare Romanian ei, Megleno-Romanian ieľ.

eali.etymology: From Latin illae, nominative feminine plural of ille. Compare Romanian ele.

atsea.etymology: From the Vulgar Latin *eccum illa, feminine singular of *eccum ille, from Latin eccum + ille. Compare Romanian acea.

hertu.etymology: Probably from a Vulgar Latin root *fertus, contraction of *fervitus for the past participle of Latin ferveō, fervere, as with the Daco-Romanian equivalent fiert. Compare also the Apulian (dialect of Italy) fiersetu.

utsid.etymology: From Latin occīdō. Compare Romanian ucide, ucid.

ngljets.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *inglaciō. Synchronically n- + gljets. Compare Romanian îngheța.

glosses_en: to marry, wed (take a wife), get married
nsor.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *inuxorō > from uxoror, from Latin uxor (“wife”). Compare Romanian însura, însor, compare also Neapolitan nzurare.

sãndzinedz.etymology: From sãndzi + -edz or from Latin sanguinō (with the Aromanian suffix -edz). Compare Romanian sângera, sângerez.

glosses_en: to pierce, penetrate, bore into, enter, pass through, bore through, perforate
pitrundu.etymology: From Latin pertundō, with metathesis. Compare Romanian pătrunde, pătrund.

strãbat.etymology: strã- + bat, or less likely a Vulgar Latin root *extrabattō, from Latin battuō. Compare Romanian străbate, străbat.

treambur.etymology: From Late Latin tremulō, from Latin tremulus, from tremō. Compare Romanian tremura, tremur.

ligãturã.etymology: From leg + -turã or from Late Latin ligātura, from Latin ligō. Compare Romanian legătură.

scap.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *excappō, a verb based on Late Latin cappa (“cloak”). Compare Romanian scap, scăpa.

cheadicã.etymology: From Latin pedica. Compare Romanian piedică.

ncheadic.etymology: From Latin impedicō. Compare Romanian împiedica, împiedic.

ndultsescu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *indulcēscō, *indulcīre, derived from Latin dulcem (“sweet”, adjective). Compare Romanian îndulci.

nflurescu.etymology: From n- + Latin flōrēscō (also Late Latin flōriō). Compare Romanian înflori.

glosses_en: to experience, undergo (something bad, unpleasant, unexpected)
pãtsãscu.etymology: From Latin patior. Compare Romanian pățesc.

pãtedz.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *batizō, from Ecclesiastical Latin Late Latin baptīzō, from Ancient Greek βαπτίζω (baptízō). Compare Romanian boteza, botez; cf. also Albanian pagëzoj.

lucredz.etymology: Probably from Latin lucror with the Aromanian suffix -edz, or less likely ultimately from Latin lūcubrō. Compare Romanian lucra, lucrez.

minciunedz.etymology: From minciunã + -edz or from a Vulgar Latin root *mentionō (with the Aromanian suffix -edz), probably ultimately from an alteration of Latin mentior (past participle mentītus) through the influence of mentiō. Compare Romanian minciună.

shcurtedz.etymology: From Late Latin excurtō + -edz, the former from Latin curtō.

mput.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin *imputiō or *putiō with a prefix later added, from Latin puteō. Compare Romanian împuți, împut, puți, put.

glosses_en: to walk, stroll, go for a walk, wander, mosey
priimnu.etymology: From Latin perambulō. Compare Romanian plimba, plimb.

mardzinã.etymology: From Latin marginem, accusative singular of margō. Compare Romanian margine.

acats.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *accaptiō, compare Romanian agăța, acăța.

fãrnu.etymology: From Latin frēnum. Compare Romanian frâu.

madzãre.etymology: Possibly a substrate Paleo-Balkanic word. Compare Romanian mazăre, Albanian modhull.

dzem.etymology: From Latin gemō. Compare Daco-Romanian geme, gem.

dzeamit.etymology: From Latin gemitus. Compare Romanian geamăt, Albanian gjëmë.

alãxescu.etymology: From Greek αλλάζω (allázo) (with the Aromanian suffix -escu).

aspindzur.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *expendiolō, ultimately from Latin pendō. Compare Romanian spânzura, spânzur, also Italian spenzolare, spenzolo.

spindzur.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *expendiolō, ultimately from Latin pendō. Compare Romanian spânzura, spânzur, also Italian spenzolare, spenzolo.

dzeamin.etymology: From Latin geminus. Compare Romanian geamăn.

poarcã.etymology: From Latin porca. Compare Romanian poarcă.

purtsel.etymology: From Late Latin porcellus, diminutive of Latin porcus. Compare Romanian purcel.

purtseauã.etymology: From Late Latin porcella (“female piglet”), from porcellus (“piglet”), diminutive of Latin porcus (“pig”). Compare Romanian purcea.

foamitã.etymology: From foami, possibly resulting from an originally unusual plural formation; another possibility is influence from Latin fomes, fomitem (“tinder”). Compare Romanian foamete.

cochil.etymology: Compare Romanian copil, Megleno-Romanian cupilaș, Albanian kopil, Byzantine Greek κόπελος (kópelos). Alternatively an ultimately paleo-Balkan substratum word.

auã.etymology: From Latin ūva. Compare obsolete Daco-Romanian auă.

nfash.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *infasciō or n- + Late Latin fasciō, from Latin fascia. Compare Romanian înfășa, înfăș.

roatã.etymology: From Latin rota. Compare Romanian roată.

dreptu.etymology: From Late Latin drictus; see there for further etymology. Compare Daco-Romanian drept.

cãtsãl.etymology: From Latin catellus. Compare Romanian cățel.

cãtsauã.etymology: From Latin catella. Compare Portuguese cadela and Romanian cățea.

unã.etymology: From Latin ūna, feminine of ūnus.

vindic.etymology: From Latin vindicō. Compare Romanian vindeca, vindec.

ncarcu.etymology: From ãn + Late Latin carricō, from Latin carrus. Compare Romanian încărca, încarc, compare also Albanian ngarkoj.

ãncarcu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *incarricāre, from Late Latin carricō, from Latin carrus. Compare Romanian încărca, încarc.

discarcu.etymology: From Late Latin discarricō, from carricō, from Latin carrus. Compare Romanian descărca, descarc.

tserbu.etymology: From Latin cervus. Compare Romanian cerb, Megleno-Romanian tserb.

purcãreatsã.etymology: From Late Latin porcāricia, from Latin porcus (“pig”). By surface analysis, porcu + -ãreatsã. Compare Romanian porcăreață.

giuncu.etymology: From Latin juvencus, iuvencus. Compare Romanian junc, Sicilian jencu.

steauã.etymology: From Latin stella, from Proto-Italic *stērolā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂stḗr. Compare to Daco-Romanian stea.

ntsileg.etymology: From Latin intelligō, variant of intellegō. Compare Daco-Romanian înțelege, înțeleg.

ndreptu.etymology: From Latin dīrēctus, probably from Vulgar Latin *dērēctus (or through a syncopated variant Late Latin drictus), and with the prefix n- added later within Aromanian. Compare Romanian drept.

ntsep.etymology: From Latin incipiō. Compare Romanian începe, încep.

uiar.etymology: Either from oai + -ar or from Vulgar Latin *oviārius (a root), from Latin ovis. Compare Romanian oier.

trifoljiu.etymology: From Latin trifolium. Compare Romanian trifoi.

glosses_en: to crop, mow, shear, trim, prune
tundu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *tondō, variant of Latin tondeō. Compare Romanian tunde, tund.

suflit.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin *sufflitum, from Latin sufflō, from flō (“to breathe”). Compare Romanian suflet.

lishor.etymology: From a hypothetical (perhaps Proto-Romanian) intermediate *lieu or *ljiu, from Latin levis + the diminutive suffix -shor. Compare Romanian ușor.

ljiushor.etymology: From a hypothetical (perhaps Proto-Romanian) intermediate *lieu or *ljiu, from Latin levis + the diminutive suffix -shor. Compare Romanian ușor.

trandafilã.etymology: From Greek τριαντάφυλλο (triantáfyllo). Compare Romanian trandafir, Albanian trëndafil, Ukrainian троянда (trojanda).

diznjerdu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *dismerdō, a verb based on Latin merda (“faeces”). The sense evolution from "remove faeces" to "caress" appears to have occurred in the context of childcare. Compare Romanian dezmierda.

amintu.etymology: Probably from Late Latin augmentō, from Latin augmentum.

avrã.etymology: Inherited from Latin aura, itself from Ancient Greek αὔρα (aúra, “breeze, soft wind”). Compare Megleno-Romanian aură.

dzindzii.etymology: From Latin gingīva. Compare Romanian gingie.

mãseauã.etymology: From Latin maxilla. Compare Romanian măsea.

toapsec.etymology: From Latin toxicus, from Ancient Greek τοξικόν (toxikón, “arrow poison”), from τοξικός (toxikós, “pertaining to bows”), from τόξον (tóxon, “bow”).

gavrã.etymology: Probably from a Vulgar Latin root *cavula, diminutive of Late Latin cava, from Latin cavus, cavum. Compare Romanian gaură; cf. Albanian gavër.

fricã.etymology: Probably from Ancient Greek φρίκη (phríkē) or more likely Byzantine Greek φρίκη (phríkē), but the presence of the word in Istro-Romanian indicates it was a very old borrowing. Compare Romanian frică, also Albanian frikë.

bãnedz.etymology: From banã + -edz. Compare also Albanian banoj.

adilju.etymology: From Vulgar Latin adiliō or Vulgar Latin adoliō, from Latin adoleō. Compare Romanian adia, adii.

ermu.etymology: From Late Latin herēmus, erēmus, from Ancient Greek ἐρῆμος (erêmos), ἤρεμος (ḗremos).

grindinã.etymology: From Latin grandinem, accusative singular of grandō. Compare Romanian grindină.

yinar.etymology: From yin + -ar, possibly corresponding to Latin vīnārius; compare archaic Romanian vinar, Italian vinaio.

alunã.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *abellona, from Latin abellāna. Compare Romanian alună.

alunar.etymology: From alunã + -ar. Compare the obsolete and popular variant for the month of July in Daco-Romanian, alunar.

broascã tsãstoasã.etymology: From broascã ("frog") + tsestu, from Latin testum; compare testūdō (“turtle”). Compare Romanian broască țestoasă.

iuliu.etymology: Ultimately from Latin iūlius, through the intermediate of Greek Ιούλιος (Ioúlios).

septemvriu.etymology: Borrowed from Greek Σεπτέμβριος (Septémvrios), from Latin September.

puljiu.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *pulleus, from Latin pullus. Compare Romanian pui.

nuearcã.etymology: From Latin noverca. Compare also Albanian njerkë.

tsãtsã.etymology: Either an expressive creation, or from Paleo-Balkan (Indo-European), or from Late Latin titia, titta. Compare Daco-Romanian țâță, Italian tetta, zizza, French tette, Portuguese teta, Spanish teta.

mpriunã.etymology: Possibly from a Latin construction *in per una. Compare Romanian împreună.

teacã.etymology: From Latin theca, from Ancient Greek θήκη (thḗkē, “a case, box, receptacle”). Compare Romanian teacă.

calcu.etymology: From Latin calcō. Compare Romanian călca, calc.

pradã.etymology: From Latin praeda. Compare Romanian pradă.

bilescu.etymology: Probably from Latin vellō, with a change in conjugation to a Vulgar Latin form *vellescō. Compare Romanian beli, belesc.

ritsinã.etymology: From Latin rēsīna, from Ancient Greek ῥητῑ́νη (rhētī́nē). Compare Romanian rășină.

pulicar.etymology: From Latin pollicāris, from pollex. Compare Daco-Romanian policar, which was probably borrowed, at least in its main form.

pulpã.etymology: From Latin pulpa. Compare Romanian pulpă; compare also Albanian pulpë.

pãun.etymology: From Latin pāvōnem, with the variant form paun possibly coming through a Slavic intermediate. Compare Romanian păun.

pljumbu.etymology: From Latin plumbum. Compare Romanian plumb.

ncalic.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *incaballicō, from Late Latin caballicō, from Latin caballus. Compare Romanian încăleca, încalec.

coardã.etymology: From Latin chorda, from Ancient Greek χορδή (khordḗ). Compare Romanian coardă.

ngustedz.etymology: From Latin angustō, with the Aromanian suffix -edz. Compare Romanian îngusta, îngustez.

mãnicã.etymology: From Latin manica. Compare Romanian mânecă.

mãrdzeauã.etymology: From Latin margella. Compare Romanian mărgea.

ljin.etymology: From Latin līnum. Compare Romanian in.

ngljit.etymology: From Late Latin ingluttiō, from Latin gluttiō, probably with a change in conjugation later within Aromanian. Compare Romanian înghiți, înghit.

sugljits.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin *suggluttiō probably from an alteration of Latin singultō, from singultus with the prefix sub-. The (Vulgar) Latin was probably influenced by gluttiō. Compare Romanian sughița, sughiț, Sicilian sugghiuzzari, Spanish soll

alats.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *laceus, from Latin laqueus. Compare Romanian laț.

cupã.etymology: From Late Latin cuppa, from Latin cūpa, possibly partly from Greek κούπα (koúpa). Compare Romanian cupă.

cucutã.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *cucūta, from Latin cicūta. Compare Romanian cucută; compare also Albanian kukutë.

creastã.etymology: From Latin crista. Compare Romanian creastă.

cãlãrets.etymology: From Late Latin caballāricius, from Latin caballus (“horse”). By surface analysis, cal + -ãrets. Compare Romanian călăreț, Albanian kalorës.

glosses_en: mounted, astride of, on horseback, ahorse
cãlar.etymology: From Late Latin caballāris, caballārem, ultimately from Latin caballus (“horse”). Another possibility is caballārius. Compare Romanian călare.

glosses_en: mounted, astride of, on horseback, ahorse
ncãlar.etymology: From n- + Late Latin caballāris, ultimately from Latin caballus (“horse”). Another possibility is caballārius. Compare Romanian călare.

furtu.etymology: From Latin fūrtum. Compare Romanian furt.

Crãciun.etymology: Probably from Latin creātiōnem, accusative of creātiō (“creation”). See more at Romanian Crăciun.

lunjinedz.etymology: From lunjinã or possibly from Latin lūminō with the Aromanian suffix -edz. Compare Romanian lumina, luminez.

lutseafir.etymology: From Latin lūciferum, accusative singular of lūcifer. Compare Romanian luceafăr.

nã.etymology: From Vulgar Latin nīs, from Latin nos. Compare Romanian ne (older form nă).

lapti.etymology: From Late Latin lactem, from Latin lac. Compare Romanian lapte.

angan.etymology: From Vulgar Latin or Late Latin ingannō (“to trick, deceive, mock, ridicule”) (attested in a gloss), from Latin *ganno or Latin ganniō. Compare Romanian îngâna, îngân (“imitate, mimic, parody; delude oneself, mix up”). The semantics of this

malj.etymology: From Latin malleus. Compare Romanian mai.

plaghe.etymology: From Latin plāga. Compare Albanian plagë, Romanian plagă.

viare.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *vēra, from Latin vēr (“spring”). Compare Romanian vară.

moali.etymology: From Latin mollis, mollem. Compare Romanian moale.

rosh.etymology: From Latin russus or roseus. Compare Romanian roș (regional).

pleng.etymology: From Latin plangō. Compare Daco-Romanian plânge, plâng.

nhir.etymology: From n- + hir, or from a Vulgar Latin *infīlō, from Latin fīlum. Compare Romanian înfira, înfir.

-tati.etymology: From Latin -tātem, accusative of -tās. Compare Romanian -tate.

sartsinã.etymology: From Latin sarcina. Compare Romanian sarcină.

flãmburã.etymology: Probably from or related to Greek φλάμμουρος (flámmouros). Compare Romanian flamură, also Albanian flamur.

Arbinishia.etymology: Compare Old Albanian arbër, arbën, cf. the related Arbëresh (Albanian arbërisht), Greek αρβανίτικη (arvanítiki), Arvanitika, cf. also old Romanian arbănaș (“Albanian (obsolete)”).

Frãntsia.etymology: Definite form of Frãntsii; -a (feminine definite article) added on.

Arusia.etymology: Definite form of Arusii; -a (feminine definite article) added on.

Sãrghia.etymology: Definite form of Sãrghii; -a (feminine definite article) added on.

Great Britain (the United Kingdom, a kingdom and country in Northern Europe including the island of Great Britain as well as Northern Ireland on the northeastern portion of the island of Ireland)

Suidia.etymology: Definite form of Suidii; -a (feminine definite article) added on.

tsoarã.etymology: Uncertain. Possibly a substratum word of Dacian and ultimately Indo-European origin, related to Albanian sorrë, or borrowed from it; compare Daco-Romanian cioară. Also seemingly related to several Italian dialect cognates, compare Friulian

ulmu.etymology: From Latin ulmus, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁élem (“mountain elm”). Compare Romanian ulm, Sicilian urmu.

dublu.etymology: Compare Romanian dublu; cf. French double. Ultimately from Latin duplus. See also diplo, from Greek.

glosses_en: an evil spirit or ghost, sorceress ghost
strigã.etymology: From Latin strīga, from strīx, from Ancient Greek στρίξ (stríx). Compare Romanian strigă.

mãtricã.etymology: From Latin mātrīcem, accusative singular of mātrīx. Compare Romanian mătrice.

yitsauã.etymology: From Late Latin vitella, diminutive of Latin vitula (“calf, young cow”). Compare Romanian vițea.

angurã.etymology: From Greek άγκυρα (ágkyra, “anchor”), from Ancient Greek ἄγκυρα (ánkura, “anchor”).

birbicar.etymology: Either from birbec + -ar or from Vulgar Latin or Late Latin vervēcārius, from Latin vervēx. (Also attested as Medieval Latin birbicārius or berbicarius). Compare French berger, Sardinian berbecarju, berbecàlgiu, berbegarzu, Romanian berbeca

glosses_en: that which has been cooked or baked in an oven
cupturã.etymology: From Latin coctūra. Compare Romanian coptură.

pronjiu.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *pūrōnium from Latin pūs, pūris. Compare Romanian puroi.

vãltoari.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *voltoria, from Latin volutus, from volvō (“roll, tumble”). Compare Romanian vâltoare.

glosses_en: with reddish color on its head
coatsin.etymology: From Latin coccineus or coccinus. Compare Romanian coacin.

glosses_en: to roll onto a roller in a weaving loom
nvolbu.etymology: From Latin involvō. Compare Romanian învoalbe (variant învolba).

vãrvurã.etymology: From Vulgar Latin root *volvula, from Latin volvō. Compare Romanian volbură.

urãciuni.etymology: Probably from Latin ōrātiō, ōrātiōnem, corresponding to or, urari + -ciuni. Cf. also Daco-Romanian urăciune.

alumtãtor.etymology: Inherited from Latin lū̆ctātor; by surface analysis, alumtã + -tor. Cognate with Romanian luptător.

ntindu.etymology: n- + tindu or possibly Latin intendō. Compare Romanian întinde, întind.

timsu.etymology: Probably from Latin tensus. Compare Romanian tins.

timtu.etymology: Probably from Latin tentus, variant of tensus.

lundzescu.etymology: From lungu, or possibly from Latin longīscō. Compare Romanian lungi, lungesc.

arburi.etymology: From Latin arborem f. Compare Daco-Romanian arbore.

cupaci.etymology: Compare Romanian copac, Istro-Romanian copaț ‘thicket, brushwood’, probably from Albanian kopaç ‘treestump’ or less likely cognate to it as a Balkan substratum root. Compare also Slavic kopati, which may be the ultimate origin of both.

cãrpã.etymology: From a South Slavic language, ultimately from Proto-Slavic *kъrpa. Compare Romanian cârpă.

prusopi.etymology: Derived from Byzantine Greek πρόσωπον (prósōpon, “face”). Compare Romanian prosop.

ashclji.etymology: From Late Latin ascla, from Latin assula. Compare Romanian așchie.

pulj.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *pulleus, from Latin pullus. Compare Romanian pui.

glosses_en: to spend or pass the time
pitrec.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *pertraiciō, from Latin per- + traiciō. Compare Romanian petrece, petrec.

spãntic.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *expanticō (“to burst”) (compare Romanian spinteca, spintec, Venetan spantegar (“to bust; scatter, sprinkle”), Calabrian spantecare ("to open")), from Latin pantices (“bowels”), plural of pantex; cf. pãnticã.

frimintu.etymology: Probably from Latin fermentō. Less likely from a Vulgar Latin *fragmentō, from fragmentum. Compare Romanian frământa, frământ.

glosses_en: money amassed and put aside for old age

broatic.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *brothācus (with a later change of declension), from Ancient Greek βροτάχος (brotákhos) < βάτραχος (bátrakhos). Compare Romanian brotac, broatec, Albanian bretk, bretkosë.

fãric.etymology: From Latin fabricō (which originally had to do with the forging of iron); another possibility it to a Vulgar Latin root *ferricō, from ferrum (compare Old French enfergier). Compare Romanian fereca, ferec.

glosses_en: to share, distribute, apportion, assign, dole, impart
mpartu.etymology: From Late Latin impartiō (variant of impertiō), from Latin partiō. Compare Romanian împărți, împart.

afoarã.etymology: From Latin ād forās. Compare Spanish afuera, Portuguese afora, Romanian afară.

cufurescu.etymology: From Latin conforiō, from foriō, from foria (“diarrhea”), with the Aromanian suffix -escu or possibly through a late Vulgar Latin form *conforēscō, as with many fourth conjugation verbs. Compare Romanian cufuri, cufuresc.

astraptu.etymology: Past participle of astrag. Possibly corresponds to Latin extractus.

glosses_en: past participle of astrag (invariant form used with "to have" in verb constructions)

boatsi.etymology: From Latin vōcem, accusative singular of vōx. Compare Romanian boace, Sicilian buci.

aoatsi.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *ad-hacce (from Latin hac) or *ad-hocce (from Latin hoc). Compare Romanian auace.

aoa.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *ad hac, from Latin ad + hac. Compare Megleno-Romanian ua.

milanculii.etymology: From Greek μελαγχολία (melancholía), itself from Ancient Greek μελαγχολία (melankholía).

glosses_en: to bemoan, bewail, lament, mourn for
butsescu.etymology: From boatsi or from a Vulgar Latin root *vōcescō, *vōcīre, from *vōceō, *vōceāre, from Latin vōx, possibly influenced by vāgiō. Compare Romanian boci, bocesc; cf. also Italian bociare, Spanish vocear.

glosses_en: keen (prolonged wail for a dead person)
boatsit.etymology: From butsescu or boatsi + -it, or possibly from a Vulgar Latin root *vōcitum, ultimately from Latin vōx. Compare Romanian bocet.

bureati.etymology: From Latin bōlētus, probably through a Vulgar Latin root *boletis. Ultimately from Ancient Greek βωλίτης (bōlítēs). Compare Romanian burete.

sãmtu.etymology: From Latin sānctus. Compare Romanian sânt.

blãncu.etymology: From Slavic obląku, oblonku. Compare Romanian oblânc, cf. Slovene oblúk.

apuc.etymology: Possibly from metathesis of a Vulgar Latin aucupō, from Latin aucupor. Other theories suggest Latin occupō, with meaning influenced by or confused with the former. Compare Romanian apuca, apuc.

cãshtigã.etymology: From a derivative of Latin castīgō (“to chastise, reprove; correct, amend”), cf. cãshtigari. Compare Romanian câștiga.

glosses_en: the act of caring for, worrying about, giving attention to
to give or devote attention to
cãshtighedz.etymology: From Latin castīgō (“reprove, reprimand; correct, amend”), with the Aromanian suffix -edz, or from cãshtigã. Compare Romanian câștiga, with an ultimately different semantic development. However, a regional meaning can be found closer to tha

madzãri.etymology: Possibly a substrate Paleo-Balkanic word. Compare Romanian mazăre, Albanian modhull. Alternatively, a borrowing from the Albanian.

bizelji.etymology: Probably from Ottoman Turkish بزلیه (bezelye). Compare Albanian bizele.

cadenã.etymology: Ultimately from Latin catēna, through the intermediate of another language; compare Venetan cadéna, Italian catena. Cf. also cãtinã, which may have been inherited from the same source.

cãtinã.etymology: Possibly from Latin catēna. Cf. Romanian cătină. See also cadenã.

schinari.etymology: From Late Latin spīnālis, from Latin spīna. Compare Romanian spinare, Tarantino spinale.

cãtinar.etymology: Compare Bulgarian катинар (katinar), катанец (katanec) (< Italian catenaccio), also Catalan cadenat, French cadenas. Ultimately from Latin catēna; cf. catēnārius and catēnātus.

glosses_en: to advance, progress, thrive, increase (in number, volume, etc.)
custã.etymology: From Latin cōnstat, third-person singular present indicative of cōnstō (with the variant form coming from the first-person). Compare dated/regional Daco-Romanian custa, custă.

pãljur.etymology: From Latin paliūrus, from Ancient Greek παλίουρος (palíouros). Compare Romanian păliur.

oaspi.etymology: From Latin hospes. Compare Daco-Romanian oaspete (variant oaspe).

uspets.etymology: From Latin hospitium. Compare Romanian ospăț.

filipsescu.etymology: Possibly ultimately from Ancient Greek φίλος (phílos).

glosses_en: to welcome, treat, receive hospitably, provide hospitality
to feast, banquet, regale, serve food or a feast
uspitedz.etymology: From Late Latin hospitō (with the Aromanian suffix -edz), from Latin hospes. Compare Romanian ospăta, ospătez.

cheali.etymology: From Latin pellis, pellem. Compare Romanian piele.

cheaptin.etymology: From Latin pectinō. Compare Romanian pieptăna, pieptăn.

chiaptini.etymology: From Latin pectinem. Compare Romanian pieptene.

cheaptini.etymology: From Latin pecten, pectinem. Compare Romanian pieptene.

cheatrã.etymology: From Latin petra, from Ancient Greek πέτρα (pétra) Compare Romanian piatră.

hascu.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *cascō, from Ancient Greek χάσκω (kháskō, “to yawn, gape”). Compare Romanian căsca, casc, Sardinian cascare, cascai.

cinushi.etymology: From a Vulgar Latin root *cinusia (“ash”), from Latin cinus, a less common variant of cinis. Compare Daco-Romanian cenușă, Megleno-Romanian tșănușă.

cljai.etymology: From Latin clāvis, clāvem. Compare Daco-Romanian cheie.

glosses_en: to mean, signify (have a specific meaning)

cioarã.etymology: Uncertain. Possibly a substratum word of Dacian and ultimately Indo-European origin, related to Albanian sorrë, or borrowed from it; compare Daco-Romanian cioară. Also seemingly related to several Italian dialect cognates, compare Friulian

coarnã.etymology: From Latin corna, plural of cornum, cornus (“cornel, dogwood”), reinterpreted as a feminine singular. Compare Romanian coarnă.

mãtasi.etymology: From Latin mataxa, from Ancient Greek μέταξα (métaxa). Compare Romanian mătase.

gutunjiu.etymology: From Latin cotōneus, from cotōneum, from Ancient Greek κυδώνιον (kudṓnion). Compare Romanian gutui, Sicilian cutugnu.

gutunj.etymology: From Latin cotōneus, from cotōneum, from Ancient Greek κυδώνιον (kudṓnion). Compare Romanian gutui.

proaspit.etymology: From Ancient Greek πρόσφατος (prósphatos), possibly through a regional Vulgar Latin intermediate *prospetus. Compare Megleno-Romanian proaspit, Daco-Romanian proaspăt.

vãcar.etymology: Inherited from Early Medieval Latin vaccārius. Compare Romanian văcar.

turtã.etymology: From Latin turta. Thought to derive from Latin tŏrta f (“twisted”), but this is phonologically problematic. Compare Romanian turtă.

cumãndu.etymology: From Latin commandāre, variant of commendāre. Compare Romanian comând, comânda.

crishtinãtati.etymology: From crishtin + -ãtati or from Late Latin Christiānitās, Christiānitātem, from Latin Christiānus (“Christian”). Compare Romanian creștinătate.

-ãtati.etymology: From Latin -itātem, accusative of -itās. Compare Romanian -ătate.

cripiturã.etymology: crep + -turã, or from Late Latin crepātūra, from Latin crepō. Compare Romanian crăpătură.

bunãtati.etymology: From Latin bonitās, bonitātem, corresponding to bun + -ãtati. Compare Romanian bunătate.

nibun.etymology: From ni- + bun. Compare Romanian nebun.

scãntealji.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *scintilia or *scantilia, from Latin scintilla. Compare Romanian scânteie.

rãnji.etymology: From Latin arānea (“spiderweb”). Compare Daco-Romanian râie, Megleno-Romanian rănă, Galician raña, cf. also Italian rogna.

arãnji.etymology: From Latin arānea, from or akin to Ancient Greek ἀράχνη (arákhnē). Compare Romanian râie.

arãnjos.etymology: From arãnji + -os. Compare Romanian râios. Cf. also Latin arāneōsus.

aranã.etymology: From South Slavic (cf. Serbo-Croatian ра̏на/rȁna, Bulgarian рана (rana)), from Proto-Slavic *rana. Compare Daco-Romanian rană.

ranã.etymology: From South Slavic (cf. Serbo-Croatian ра̏на/rȁna, Bulgarian рана (rana)), from Proto-Slavic *rana. Compare Daco-Romanian rană.

arãnescu.etymology: From Proto-Slavic *raniti. Compare Romanian răni, rănesc.

crutsi.etymology: From Latin crux, crucem. Compare Daco-Romanian cruce.

bisearicã.etymology: From Latin basilica, from Ancient Greek βασιλική (basilikḗ). Compare Romanian biserică.
